questions.question: In Shakespeare's tragedy 'Othello', who is Othello's deceitful ensign who meticulously orchestrates his tragic downfall?
questions.explanation: Iago poisons Othello mind against Desdemona through cunning villainy.

questions.question: Which melancholic lord in 'As You Like It' delivers the famous monologue beginning 'All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players'?
questions.explanation: Lord Jaques delivers the Seven Ages of Man speech in Act 2 Scene 7.

questions.question: In Shakespeare's 'Twelfth Night', what ridiculous attire is the pompous steward Malvolio tricked into wearing by Maria's forged letter?
options: A fool motley coat and cap
questions.explanation: Malvolio appears smiling and cross-gartered in yellow stockings to please Olivia.

questions.question: Select the correct indirect narration: He said, 'I have passed the examination.'
options: He said that I had passed the entire examination.
He said that he had passed the examination.
He told that he had passed the examination successfully.
He said that he has passed the difficult examination.
questions.explanation: Present perfect tense changes to past perfect tense in indirect speech.

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: The officer said to the soldiers, 'Halt!'
options: The officer commanded the soldiers to halt.
The officer requested the soldiers to halt immediately.
The officer said the soldiers to halt at once.
The officer told to the soldiers that they must halt.
questions.explanation: Military orders are transformed using commanded or ordered followed by to infinitive.

questions.question: Which historical chronicles served as William Shakespeare's chief source for his English history plays and 'Macbeth'?
questions.explanation: Raphael Holinshed Chronicles published in 1577 was his main historical source.

questions.question: Which Romantic poet praised William Shakespeare as the supreme exemplar of 'Negative Capability' in an 1817 letter?
questions.explanation: John Keats named Shakespeare as possessing Negative Capability so enormously.

questions.question: In P.B. Shelley's elegy 'Adonais', in which historic cemetery in Rome is John Keats buried near the pyramid of Cestius?
questions.explanation: Keats is buried in the Protestant Cemetery in Rome where Shelley ashes were also later placed.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form: She said, 'Alas! I am undone.'
options: She exclaimed with sorrow that she was undone.
She said with sorrow that I am utterly undone.
She exclaimed with joy that she was finally undone.
She cried out in grief that she had been undone.
questions.explanation: Alas expresses grief and transforms into exclaimed with sorrow followed by past simple.

questions.question: Choose the correct antonym of the word 'METICULOUS':
questions.explanation: Meticulous means taking immense care with details; its opposite is negligent or careless.

questions.question: 'I met a traveller from an antique land / Who said: Two vast and trunkless legs of stone / Stand in the desert' opens which sonnet by P.B. Shelley?
questions.explanation: Ozymandias published in 1818 reflects on the fleeting nature of political power.

questions.question: In which body of water did P.B. Shelley drown in July 1822 when his boat Don Juan was caught in a storm?
options: The Bay of Naples in southern Italy
questions.explanation: Shelley drowned in the Gulf of Spezia off Livorno on 8 July 1822 at age twenty-nine.

questions.question: 'Thou wast not born for death, immortal Bird! / No hungry generations tread thee down' is addressed to the bird in which ode by John Keats?
questions.explanation: Keats contrasts mortal human suffering with the immortal art of the nightingale.

questions.question: Select the closest synonym for the word 'BENEVOLENT':
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly, matching compassionate.

questions.question: What is the exact antonym of the word 'AFFLUENT'?
questions.explanation: Affluent means having a great deal of money; impoverished means made poor.

questions.question: Which celebrated literary ballad by John Keats takes its title from a fifteenth-century French poem by Alain Chartier?
options: Isabella; or, The Pot of Basil
The Eve of St. Mark in Spring
questions.explanation: Keats borrowed the title from Alain Chartier courtly French lyric.

questions.question: What famous inscription did John Keats request to be carved upon his tombstone without his name?
options: Beauty was his True Life and Truth his Beauty
A Young Poet of Truth and Untouched Beauty
Here lies One Whose Name was writ in Water
Gone to the Realm of Uncertainties and Doubts
questions.explanation: Keats dictated this modest epitaph reflecting his feelings of unfulfilled ambition.

questions.question: Which poem by Alfred Lord Tennyson commemorates the doomed cavalry charge at the Battle of Balaclava in the Crimean War?
options: The Charge of the Heavy Brigade
The Charge of the Light Brigade
The Revenge; A Ballad of the Fleet
questions.explanation: Tennyson wrote the famous lines Into the valley of Death / Rode the six hundred in 1854.

questions.question: Choose the correct synonym of the verb 'AMELIORATE':
questions.explanation: Ameliorate signifies making something bad or unsatisfactory better, meaning improve.

questions.question: What is the antonym of the word 'BELLICOSE'?
questions.explanation: Bellicose means demonstrating aggression and willingness to fight; peaceable is its antonym.

questions.question: What is the collective title of Alfred Lord Tennyson's cycle of twelve narrative poems retelling the legend of King Arthur and his knights?
questions.explanation: Idylls of the King published between 1859 and 1885 retells Arthurian legend in blank verse.

questions.question: Ebenezer Scrooge, the reformed miser visited by three Christmas spirits, is the central protagonist of which work by Charles Dickens?
questions.explanation: A Christmas Carol in Prose published in 1843 is Dickens beloved holiday novella.

questions.question: The interminable Chancery suit 'Jarndyce and Jarndyce' provides the satirical framework for which Charles Dickens novel?
questions.explanation: Bleak House published in 1852-53 severely satirizes the corrupt Court of Chancery.

questions.question: Choose the statement that correctly distinguishes 'COMPLIMENT' from 'COMPLEMENT':
options: Compliment means something that completes; complement means polite praise.
Both words denote an expression of admiration or flatter in speech.
Both words signify an addition that improves something significantly.
Compliment means polite praise; complement means something that completes.
questions.explanation: Compliment with i is polite praise; complement with e means completing a set.

questions.question: A separate introductory section of a literary, dramatic, or musical work is called a:
questions.explanation: A prologue is an opening section providing background or context to a drama or novel.

questions.question: 'Five years have past; five summers, with the length / Of five long winters!' is the opening line of which masterpiece poem by William Wordsworth?
questions.explanation: Wordsworth opens Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey revisiting the banks of the Wye.

questions.question: In 'The World Is Too Much with Us', Wordsworth laments modern commercialism and longs to see which sea god rising from the waters?
questions.explanation: Wordsworth writes Have sight of Proteus rising from the sea or hear old Triton blow his wreathed horn.

questions.question: Which family member kept the detailed 'Grasmere Journals' that frequently provided William Wordsworth with poetic inspiration?
questions.explanation: His sister Dorothy Wordsworth journals recorded observations of daffodils and country life.

questions.question: One who possesses unlimited power and authority is described as:
questions.explanation: Omnipotent means having unlimited power; omniscient means all-knowing.

questions.question: An account of a person's life written by that person himself or herself is an:
questions.explanation: An autobiography is a self-written life history; biography is written by another.

questions.question: Which 1935 verse play by T.S. Eliot dramatizes the assassination of Archbishop Thomas Becket in Canterbury Cathedral in 1170?
questions.explanation: Commissioned for the Canterbury Festival, it portrays Becket martyrdom resisting royal authority.

questions.question: In his seminal 1919 essay 'Tradition and the Individual Talent', T.S. Eliot compared the mind of the mature poet to which scientific catalyst?
options: A fine grain of pure gold
questions.explanation: Eliot famously analogies the creative process to sulphurous acid formed in the presence of platinum.

questions.question: In which famous essay of Elia does Charles Lamb humorously describe the Chinese peasant Bo-bo accidentally burning down a cottage?
questions.explanation: A Dissertation upon Roast Pig recounts the mythical discovery of the delicacy of roast pig.

questions.question: An inscription or phrase written on a tombstone or monument in memory of a deceased person is an:
questions.explanation: An epitaph is an inscription engraved on a tombstone or monument.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to beat about the bush'?
options: To clear thick bushes in an overgrown garden
To search vigorously for wild game in the woods
To avoid discussing the main topic directly
To strike someone repeatedly with a walking stick
questions.explanation: To beat about the bush means approaching an issue in an evasive or roundabout manner.

questions.question: Which 1808 pioneering anthology compiled by Charles Lamb restored critical appreciation for neglected Elizabethan and Jacobean dramatists?
options: Classic Plays of the Ancient London Authors
The Dramatic Mirror of English Authors
questions.explanation: Specimens of English Dramatic Poets revived interest in Marlowe and Webster.

questions.question: Gabriel Oak, Bathsheba Everdene, and Farmer Boldwood are the central characters in which Wessex novel by Thomas Hardy?
options: A Pair of Blue Eyes in Cornwall
Under the Greenwood Tree in Wessex
questions.explanation: Far from the Madding Crowd published in 1874 was Hardy first major critical and commercial triumph.

questions.question: Which poem by Thomas Hardy, published on 31 December 1900, reflects on the close of the nineteenth century through an aged singing thrush?
questions.explanation: Originally titled By the Century Deathbed, the poem finds a frail hope in the thrush song.

questions.question: The idiomatic phrase 'to leave no stone unturned' signifies:
options: To destroy valuable historical monuments in time of war
To wander aimlessly across rocky terrain without direction
To engage in strenuous masonry or building work with rocks
To try every possible means to achieve an objective
questions.explanation: It means using every available resource or method to achieve a desired goal.

questions.question: What does the expression 'through thick and thin' mean?
options: Eating heavy rich foods and thin light broths alternately
Walking across deep muddy ground and dense forests
Under all conditions, both pleasant and difficult
Gradually gaining and losing personal physical weight
questions.explanation: It signifies remaining steadfast in loyalty and support through good and bad times.

questions.question: Which famous poem by Robert Frost opens with the line 'Something there is that doesn't love a wall'?
questions.explanation: Mending Wall published in North of Boston in 1914 explores natural and human barriers.

questions.question: Robert Frost delivered his poem 'The Gift Outright' from memory at the presidential inauguration of which U.S. President in January 1961?
questions.explanation: Unable to read his newly written poem due to snow glare, Frost recited The Gift Outright from memory.

questions.question: In Kamala Das's celebrated poem 'The Dance of the Eunuchs', what physical atmosphere mirrors the sterile anguish of the dancers?
options: A dry, sultry wind followed by meager rain
A calm autumn sunset by the tropical seaside
A chilling winter breeze under gloomy clouds
A torrential downpour during the monsoon season
questions.explanation: The harsh heat and meager raindrops symbolize the sterile and unfulfilled passion of the eunuchs.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He is senior ______ me in service by four years.
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives ending in -ior like senior junior superior take preposition to not than.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The poor laborer died ______ cholera after drinking contaminated water.
questions.explanation: One dies of a disease like cholera or malaria, but dies from overwork or a wound.

questions.question: In Mulk Raj Anand's tragic novel 'Two Leaves and a Bud' (1937), what is the geographical and occupational setting of Gangu's exploitation?
questions.explanation: The novel depicts the brutal exploitation of poor coolies on a British-managed Assam tea estate.

questions.question: What is the name of Ernest Hemingway's minimalist aesthetic principle that only one-eighth of a story's meaning should appear on the surface?
questions.explanation: Hemingway Theory of Omission or Iceberg Theory leaves deeper meaning implicit under simple prose.

questions.question: In Nissim Ezekiel's satirical poem 'Goodbye Party for Miss Pushpa T.S.', Miss Pushpa is preparing to travel abroad for:
questions.explanation: The speaker announces in Indian English that Miss Pushpa is departing for foreign to improve her prospect.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: The security guard prevented the stranger ______ entering the premises.
questions.explanation: The verb prevent is standardly followed by from plus gerund.

questions.question: Which negative prefix is attached to the adjective 'PURE' to form its opposite meaning?
questions.explanation: Words beginning with p frequently take the negative prefix im- to form impure.

questions.question: Walt Whitman broke away from traditional European poetic meter and rhyme, earning him title of the father of American:
questions.explanation: Whitman pioneered modern free verse using cadence, parallelism, and cataloging in Leaves of Grass.

questions.question: The Bundren family's arduous journey across Mississippi to bury their deceased mother Addie is recounted in which William Faulkner novel?
questions.explanation: As I Lay Dying in 1930 uses fifteen distinct narrators across fifty-nine interior monologues.

questions.question: Which major narrative poem by Geoffrey Chaucer, composed in rime royale, tells the tragic romance of two lovers during the siege of Troy?
questions.explanation: Troilus and Criseyde based on Boccaccio Filostrato is Chaucer greatest finished narrative poem.

questions.question: Which suffix is added to the noun 'HERO' to derive an adjective signifying noble courage?
questions.explanation: Hero takes the suffix -ic to form the descriptive adjective heroic.

questions.question: What is the proper negative prefix for the adjective 'OBEDIENT'?
questions.explanation: Obedient takes the negative prefix dis- to form disobedient.

questions.question: In 'The Canterbury Tales', which lively pilgrim from near Bath has had five husbands and discourses at length on female sovereignty in marriage?
questions.explanation: The Wife of Bath Alison delivers a spirited prologue arguing that women desire mastery over husbands.

questions.question: Dorothea Brooke, an idealistic young woman who enters an unhappy marriage with the pedantic scholar Edward Casaubon, is the heroine of:
questions.explanation: Dorothea marital disillusionment with Casaubon forms the primary emotional arc of Middlemarch.

questions.question: Which 1859 novel was George Eliot's first published full-length novel, portraying the carpenter Adam Bede and the dairymaid Hetty Sorrel?
questions.explanation: Adam Bede established Mary Ann Evans reputation as an exceptional Victorian realistic novelist.

questions.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence from the following options:
options: Each of the participant was given a certificate.
Each of the participants was given a certificate.
Each of the participant were given a certificate.
Each of the participants were given a certificate.
questions.explanation: Each of takes a plural noun followed by a singular verb in standard grammar.

questions.question: Transform the sentence into a negative sentence without changing meaning: 'He is as cunning as a fox.'
options: A fox is as cunning as he is in cleverness.
A fox is distinctly less cunning than he is.
He is not more cunning than any fox in nature.
A fox is not more cunning than he is.
questions.explanation: Equative positive comparison transforms into comparative negative asserting equal cunning.

questions.question: Eddie Carbone, a Brooklyn longshoreman whose unacknowledged passion for his niece Catherine destroys him, is the protagonist of which Arthur Miller play?
questions.explanation: A View from the Bridge in 1955 follows Eddie Carbone tragic jealousy involving Italian cousins.

questions.question: In Arthur Miller's 'Death of a Salesman', what are the names of Willy and Linda Loman's two grown sons?
questions.explanation: Biff, the former high school football star, and Happy, the assistant, are Willy sons.

questions.question: Which 1973 novel by Toni Morrison focuses on the community of the Bottom and the complex friendship between Nel Wright and Sula Peace?
questions.explanation: Sula set in the Bottom explores female bonding, individuality, and social expectations.

questions.question: Transform the rhetorical interrogative sentence into an assertive sentence: 'Who can touch pitch and not be defiled?'
options: No one can touch pitch without being defiled.
None can touch pitch and avoid being defiled completely.
Everyone can touch pitch and not be defiled at all.
Someone can easily touch pitch and be defiled forever.
questions.explanation: Rhetorical question Who can... transforms into the negative assertive No one can.

questions.question: Select the sentence with grammatically correct correlative conjunction usage:
options: No sooner had the bell rung than the children ran out.
No sooner did the bell rang than all the children ran out quickly.
No sooner had the bell rung but all the children ran out at once.
No sooner the bell had rung when the children ran out outside.
questions.explanation: No sooner is followed by auxiliary inversion had plus subject and correlates with than.

questions.question: Set in Harlem during the 1920s, which 1992 historical novel by Toni Morrison follows Joe and Violet Trace against the backdrop of the Jazz Age?
questions.explanation: Jazz published in 1992 forms the second work in Morrison historical fiction trilogy.

questions.question: 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair' spoken by the three witches in Shakespeare's 'Macbeth' is an example of which rhetorical figure of reversal?
questions.explanation: Chiasmus involves a reversal in the order of words in two parallel phrases in an ABBA pattern.

questions.question: Replacing a harsh or blunt expression with an inoffensive or mild phrase, such as saying 'passed away' instead of 'died', is called a:
questions.explanation: A euphemism substitutes an agreeable or mild expression for one that may offend or suggest unpleasantness.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that correctly employs the conjunction 'Although':
options: Although he worked hard, but he failed in the test.
Although he worked hard, he failed in the test.
Although he worked hard, yet he failed in the test.
Although he worked hard, so he failed in the test.
questions.explanation: Although should be paired with a comma or yet, but combining although with but is incorrect.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'The committee will announce the final results tomorrow.'
options: The final results are announced by the committee tomorrow.
The final results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The final results would be announced by the committee tomorrow.
The final results will announce tomorrow by the committee.
questions.explanation: Future simple passive is formed using will be plus past participle announced.

questions.question: 'Ten thousand saw I at a glance, / Tossing their heads in sprightly dance' in Wordsworth's 'Daffodils' is an example of:
questions.explanation: Ten thousand saw I at a glance is a deliberate poetic exaggeration known as hyperbole.

questions.question: 'Milton! thou shouldst be living at this hour: / England hath need of thee' in Wordsworth's sonnet 'London, 1802' is an example of:
questions.explanation: Directly addressing the deceased poet John Milton who is absent is an apostrophe.

questions.question: In the sentence 'He has five hungry mouths to feed', using 'mouths' to refer to persons is an example of which figure of speech?
questions.explanation: Synecdoche is a figure of speech in which a part of something represents the whole.

questions.question: Change the passive sentence into active voice: 'The wooden bridge was swept away by the raging flood.'
options: The raging flood was sweeping away the wooden bridge.
The raging flood swept away the wooden bridge.
The raging flood sweeps away the wooden bridge.
The raging flood had swept away the wooden bridge.
questions.explanation: Simple past passive was swept away converts into active past simple swept away.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences exhibits correct subject-verb agreement with 'Neither... nor'?
options: Neither the manager nor his assistants was present in the room.
Neither the manager nor his assistants has been present today.
Neither the manager nor his assistants is present at the meeting.
Neither the manager nor his assistants were present.
questions.explanation: In neither nor constructions, the verb agrees with the nearer subject assistants.

questions.question: In 'An Apology for Poetry' (1595), which Elizabethan poet and critic defended poetry against Stephen Gosson's Puritan attacks?
questions.explanation: Sidney defended poetry asserting that the poet never lieth because he nothing affirmeth.

questions.question: 'A little learning is a dang'rous thing; / Drink deep, or taste not the Pierian spring' is a celebrated couplet from which poem by Alexander Pope?
options: The Rape of the Lock mock epic
An Essay on Man in verse
questions.explanation: Pope published An Essay on Criticism in heroic couplets in 1711 when he was twenty-three.

questions.question: Which literary theorist and critic established the distinction between the 'scientific or referential' use and the 'emotive' use of language in 1924?
questions.explanation: I.A. Richards formulated this distinction in Principles of Literary Criticism.

questions.question: Identify the word that is correctly spelled from the choices given below:
questions.explanation: Conscientious is spelled c-o-n-s-c-i-e-n-t-i-o-u-s.

questions.question: Select the correctly spelled word from the following options:
questions.explanation: Maintenance is spelled with tenance as m-a-i-n-t-e-n-a-n-c-e.

questions.question: In 'The Function of Criticism at the Present Time' (1864), which critic defined criticism as 'a disinterested endeavour to learn and propagate the best'?
questions.explanation: Matthew Arnold championed disinterestedness and the best that is known and thought in the world.

questions.question: The English Augustan Age in literature, distinguished by formal wit, satire, and imitation of Roman models, spans approximately:
questions.explanation: The Augustan Age corresponds to the literary era of Pope, Swift, and Addison in early eighteenth century.

questions.question: Which famous poem by Thomas Gray is regarded as the pinnacle of the eighteenth-century 'Graveyard School' of poetry?
options: Ode on the Spring by Thomas Gray
Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard
Night Thoughts by Edward Young in London
The Grave by Robert Blair in Scotland
questions.explanation: Thomas Gray Elegy published in 1751 meditates on mortality among humble rural forefathers.

questions.question: Find the word with the correct spelling:
questions.explanation: Questionnaire has double n and ending aire as q-u-e-s-t-i-o-n-n-a-i-r-e.

questions.question: Identify the correctly spelled word among the following:
questions.explanation: Occurrence features double c and double r as o-c-c-u-r-r-e-n-c-e.

questions.question: The Jacobean era of English literature corresponds to the reign of which English monarch between 1603 and 1625?
questions.explanation: Jacobean is derived from Jacobus, the Latin form of James, following Elizabeth I death in 1603.

questions.question: Which three-line interlocking stanza form rhyming 'aba bcb cdc' was invented by Dante Alighieri and used in English by Shelley in 'Ode to the West Wind'?
questions.explanation: Terza rima is an Italian tercet form with chain rhyme aba bcb cdc.

questions.question: What is the term for verse written in unrhymed iambic pentameter lines, famously used by Marlowe, Shakespeare, and Milton?
questions.explanation: Blank verse is regular unrhymed iambic pentameter, the staple of English dramatic poetry.

questions.question: Select the sentence with correct punctuation in direct speech:
options: He said, Where are you going?
questions.explanation: The introductory reporting verb is set off by a comma, and punctuation stays inside quotes.

questions.question: Identify the tense of the underlined verb phrase: 'She will be preparing for her examination at this time tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: Will be preparing denotes an ongoing action in progress at a specific time in the future.
